classification.difficultyReason: Express shaded area as a fraction by recognising equal-area units within unequal-looking regions, then simplify.

content.prompt: What fraction of the shape is shaded?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12 diagram below its prompt, left aligned.
spec.description: A regular hexagon with horizontal top and bottom edges, partitioned into three congruent unshaded smaller hexagons and three congruent shaded rhombi. The smaller hexagons occupy upper-left, lower-left and centre-right positions. The shaded rhombi occupy the left vertex and the upper-right and lower-right edges.
spec.mathematics: Each smaller hexagon has the area of three of the shaded rhombi. The complete figure therefore contains twelve equal rhombus-area units, three of which are shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: The assessed shading and all original partition boundaries remain visible. No fraction, count or additional subdivision is supplied in the question figure.

answer.worked:
Split each unshaded hexagon into three equal rhombi. There are 3 shaded rhombi out of 12 equal rhombi altogether.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Shaded fraction}&=\frac{3}{12}\\&=\frac{3\div3}{12\div3}\\&=\frac{1}{4}\end{align*}$$
